As we delve into the intricacies of AI evaluation, its crucial to understand the pivotal role of events like miniCON 2025 in shaping the future of AI research and development. Multimodal AI represents a significant leap forward in artificial intelligence. Unlike traditional models that focus on a single type of data input, multimodal AI systems can integrate and process multiple forms of data simultaneously. This capability mirrors the human ability to interpret various sensory inputs, making it a powerful tool for creating more comprehensive and intuitive AI systems. For instance, a multimodal AI system could analyze a video by understanding the visual elements, interpreting the accompanying audio, and even recognizing textual content within the video. This holistic approach allows for a deeper understanding of context and enhances the AIs ability to make informed decisions. articles.title: Smart Food Market Trends 2025 : Innovation Sustainability
articles.content: Published: 2025-10-08 Innovations in smart food technologies are transforming how we preserve and manage perishable items, addressing global challenges like food waste and supply chain inefficiencies. Recent breakthroughs from research institutions and consumer electronics giants highlight practical solutions that integrate biotechnology and artificial intelligence to extend shelf life and optimize home food handling. In 2025, significant advancements have emerged in smart food preservation. Researchers from MIT and the Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology developed biodegradable silk microneedles to inject melatonin into fresh-cut crops, such as pak choy, to delay spoilage. This method extended shelf life by four days at room temperature and 10 days under refrigeration, based on tests showing reduced yellowing, weight loss, and chlorophyll degradation. Concurrently, Samsung Electronics rolled out a new lineup of smart refrigerators in March 2025, featuring enhanced AI Vision Inside that recognizes 37 food items, including processed foods, and saves up to 50 items for tailored recipe recommendations and meal planning. These models also incorporate Hybrid Cooling technology, using a Peltier module with a compressor to maintain consistent temperatures and freshness. These technologies apply to agriculture, food retail, and consumer appliances. The microneedle approach targets post-harvest preservation in farming and supply chains, minimizing waste in perishable produce without relying solely on energy-intensive refrigeration. It delivers hormones like melatonin to regulate plant physiology, preserving antioxidant activity and slowing senescence. In the home appliance sector, Samsungs refrigerators serve as smart hubs for food management, integrating AI for inventory tracking, energy optimization, and entertainment. Features like AI Vision Inside streamline meal planning, while Hybrid Cooling prevents temperature fluctuations, benefiting households by reducing spoilage and supporting sustainable practices. North America dominates the smart food market due to advanced research infrastructure and rapid adoption of AI-driven appliances. Asia-Pacific emerges as the fastest-growing region, driven by challenges in post-harvest waste and increasing demand for innovative preservation methods. articles.title: 20 New Technology Trends for 2026 Emerging Technologies 2026
articles.content: TL;DR: By 2026, technology will be driven by AI, sustainability, and intelligent automation. Agentic AI will evolve from assistance to autonomy, while green computing, edge AI, and quantum systems transform industries. Immersive tools and robotics will reshape work and design, and new careers will emerge in AI, cybersecurity, and sustainability. This article breaks down the 20 new technology trends of 2026, the opportunities they create, and the future-ready roles that will lead this era of intelligent transformation. At 8:59 a.m., a marketer opens a dashboard where an AI agent has already built, tested, and costed a campaign overnight. By 9:10, that agent has launched personalized offers across channels, adjusted spend based on real-time clicks, and written the next batch of ad copy. It does not make headlines, but it is how marketing will run in 2026: autonomous, adaptive, and always on. The challenge is pace. Systems are connecting, learning, and acting across the stack, from edge devices to cloud platforms. That speed is rewriting job scopes and team structures. The World Economic Forum projects that 23 percent of current roles will be disrupted by 2027, even as 69 million new, tech-centric roles open for those who can adapt. Explore the top new technology trends shaping 2026, from AI-driven innovation to sustainable computing and intelligent automation, transforming industries worldwide. With the start of 2026, the phrase AI assistant will sound outdated. The new reality is agentic AI, systems that can reason, plan, and act on their own. Picture an AI that not only drafts a marketing campaign but tests variations overnight, launches the top-performing version, and adjusts budgets as results come in, all before your first meeting of the day. AI is evolving from copilots that support humans to autonomous agents that handle end-to-end workflows. According to Research Nester, the autonomous AI market is projected to hit USD 11.79 billion by 2026, growing at a CAGR above 40 percent through 2035. This marks one of the latest technology trends redefining enterprise workflows, blending automation, reasoning, and adaptability. Companies deploying agentic systems report faster decisions, reduced manual errors, and continuous optimization at a scale humans alone cannot match. A logistics firm can reroute hundreds of shipments in minutes, while a financial agent adjusts portfolios in real time to hedge against volatility. Agentic AI will open up new roles for professionals who can design, monitor, and scale these intelligent agents. Success will depend on understanding how to guide AI behavior, ensure ethical use, and align outcomes with business goals. Building those skills means learning prompt design, retrieval-augmented generation, and AI governance, capabilities covered in Professional Certificate in AI and Machine Learning, which helps learners move from using AI to leading it. AI governance will move from optional to operational in 2026, quickly becoming the center of technology trends and policy conversations. With the EU AI Act taking effect in 2025 and similar laws emerging across North America and Asia-Pacific, companies will have to prove that every model they use is transparent, fair, and bias-checked. The AI governance market, valued at USD 227.6 million in 2024, is projected to reach USD 1.4 billion by 2030, making compliance one of the fastest-growing domains in AI. Organizations will transition from reactive compliance to proactive governance. Model registries, fairness audits, and explainability dashboards are already becoming standard practice across industries and will become mainstays in 2026. In sectors like healthcare and finance, where algorithmic decisions directly impact lives, meeting these benchmarks is not optional; it is essential. Governance is fast becoming a competitive advantage. Businesses that operationalize responsible AI early will not only avoid penalties but also build brand trust and investor confidence. Ethical AI frameworks will signal maturity, helping enterprises win customers and partnerships that value transparency. AI governance will create a new class of professionals who bridge technology, ethics, and regulation. Demand will rise for experts who can evaluate bias, manage model risk, and document AI decisions for accountability. Building this expertise starts with understanding how governance fits into real-world systems.
